Surah al-Qasas (The Narratives) [Meccan, except verses 52 to 55, which are Medinan, and verse 85, which was revealed at al-Juhfa during the Hijra; its verses number 88]. It was revealed after an-Naml (The Ant).

﴿Ta-Sin-Mim﴾. God knows best what He means by this.

﴿Tilka﴾ means "these," i.e., these verses, ﴿āyāt al-Kitāb﴾ (the verses of the Book), the idafa here carrying the sense of "from" (min), ﴿al-mubīn﴾ (the clear one), that which makes the truth manifest from falsehood.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 3:

﴿We recite﴾ we relate ﴿to you, from the news﴾ the report ﴿of Musa and Fir'awn, in truth﴾ the veracity ﴿for a people who believe﴾ for their sake, because they are the ones who benefit from it.

Indeed, Pharaoh exalted himself (تَعَظَّمَ) in the land (أرض مِصر, the land of Egypt), and made its people sects (شِيَعًا, factions) in his service, weakening (يَسْتَضْعِف) a group among them, who were the Children of Israel, slaughtering (يُذَبِّح) their sons, those newly born, and sparing (يَسْتَبْقِيهِنَّ أحْياء, keeping them alive) their women, because of the statement of some of the soothsayers (الكَهَنَة, sing. كاهن, kahin, soothsayer) to him: "A boy will be born among the Children of Israel who will be the cause of the end of your kingdom." ﴿Indeed, he was among the corrupters﴾ through killing and other than it.

And We intend to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and to make them the inheritors. (Recited with) *bi-tahqiq al-hamzatayn* (the two hamzas each pronounced in full, without easing either) and *ibdal al-thaniya ya'an* (replacing the second hamza with a *ya'*): *yuqtada bihim fi al-khayr* (they are followed in goodness). ﴿And make them the inheritors﴾: the kingdom of Pharaoh (*mulk Fir'awn*).

and We shall establish them in the land (the land of Egypt and al-Sham), and show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts (in another reading, "yaraa" with a yā' vowelled with a fatḥa and the rā' with a fatḥa, and the three names in the nominative) what they were wary of from them (fearing the boy who would bring an end to their kingdom at his hands).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 7:

﴿And We inspired﴾ an inspiration of inspiration (wahy ilham) or a dream, ﴿to the mother of Musa﴾, and he is the aforementioned newborn, and none knew of his birth except his sister. ﴿Suckle him, and when you fear for him, then cast him into the sea﴾, the sea meaning the Nile. ﴿And do not fear﴾ his drowning, ﴿and do not grieve﴾ at his separation from you, ﴿Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾. So she suckled him for three months without him crying, and she feared for him, so she placed him in a chest coated with pitch (qar) on the inside, prepared for him within it, closed it, and cast it into the Nile at night.

﴿So he was picked up﴾ by the family of Pharaoh, in the ark, at dawn. ﴿Family﴾ means his attendants. They placed him before Pharaoh, the ark was opened, and Musa was taken out of it while he was sucking milk from his thumb. ﴿That he might become for them﴾ in the final outcome ﴿an enemy﴾ who would kill their men, ﴿and a grief﴾ who would enslave their women. In another reading, with a damma on the ha and a sukun on the za, both forms are dialects for the verbal noun. Here the word has the meaning of the ism al-fa'il (active participle) from ḥazzanahu, like aḥzanahu (it grieved him). ﴿Indeed Pharaoh and Haman﴾, his vizier, ﴿and their hosts were sinners﴾. It comes from sin (khaṭī'ah), meaning they were disobedient, so they were punished at his hands.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 9:

﴿And the wife of Pharaoh said﴾ — and he, together with his helpers, had resolved to kill him — ﴿"[He will be] a comfort of the eye for me and for you. Do not kill him; perhaps he will benefit us, or we may take him as a son."﴾ So they obeyed her, ﴿while they did not perceive﴾ the outcome of their affair concerning him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 10:

﴿And the heart of Moses' mother became empty﴾ when she learned of his being picked up, ﴿empty﴾ of everything else, ﴿for she was about to disclose him﴾ — ﴿in-﴾ is a lightened form of the heavy (mushaddadah) in-na (indeed), and its noun is omitted, meaning: indeed she ﴿was about to disclose him﴾, i.e., that he was her son, ﴿had We not fortified her heart﴾ with patience, i.e., made it firm, ﴿that she might be of the believers﴾ who affirm the promise of Allah. The answer to ﴿lawla﴾ (had it not been) is indicated by what precedes it.

﴿And she said to his sister﴾ Maryam, ﴿"Follow him"﴾ (follow his trail until you learn his news), ﴿so she watched him from afar﴾ (she saw him from a distance), stealthily, ﴿while they did not perceive﴾ that she was his sister and that she was watching him.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 28, verse 12:

﴿And We had forbidden him the wet-nurses before﴾, that is, before his being returned to his mother; that is, We prevented him from accepting the breast of any nursing woman other than his mother, so he would not take the breast of any of the wet-nurses who were brought to him. ﴿Then his sister said﴾, ﴿"Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you"﴾, with nursing and otherwise, ﴿"and they will be sincere toward him?"﴾ When she saw their compassion toward him. The pronoun in ﴿lahu﴾ ("for him") was interpreted as referring to the kingship, as a reply to them. She was answered, and she brought his mother. So he took her breast, and she answered them regarding his acceptance of her by saying that she had a pleasant scent and pleasant milk. So he (Musa) was permitted to be nursed by her in her house, and she returned with him, as God, exalted is He, said:

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 13:

﴿So We returned him to his mother, that her eye might be comforted, and that she would not grieve, and that she would know that the promise of God is true⁠—﴾ by his meeting her ﴿and that she would not grieve﴾ at that time ﴿and that she would know that the promise of God﴾ regarding his return to her ﴿is true; but most of them﴾ i.e., the people ﴿do not know﴾ this promise, nor that this one is his sister and this one is his mother. So he remained with her until she weaned him, and [Pharaoh] paid her a wage of one dinar every day, and she took it, because it was property of the enemy (ḥarbī). Then she brought him to Pharaoh, and he was raised in his house, as God the Exalted said, relating about him, in Surat al-Shu'arā': ﴿Did We not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 14:

﴿When he reached his maturity (ashudd)﴾, and that is thirty years or thirty-three, ﴿and became firm (istawa)﴾, meaning he reached forty years, ﴿We gave him judgment (hukm)﴾, meaning wisdom, ﴿and knowledge (ilm)﴾, meaning understanding (fiqh) of the religion, before he was sent as a prophet (nabiyy). ﴿And thus﴾, as We recompensed him, ﴿We recompense the good-doers﴾ for their own selves.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 28, verse 15:**

﴿And he entered﴾ the city, Moses entered ﴿the city﴾, the city of Pharaoh, which is Memphis, after he had been absent from it for a period. ﴿At a time of heedlessness of its people﴾, at the time of al-qaylulah (the midday rest). ﴿He found in it two men fighting, one of his own faction﴾, that is, an Israelite, ﴿and the other of his enemy﴾, that is, a Qibti (Egyptian), who was conscripting the Israelite to carry firewood to Pharaoh's kitchen. ﴿So the one of his own faction called on him for help against the one of his enemy﴾. Moses said to him, "Let him go." It was said that the Qibti had said to Moses, "I was about to make him carry it upon you." ﴿So Moses struck him﴾, that is, he hit him with the full of his palm, and he was very strong and forceful. ﴿And he dispatched him﴾, he killed him, though he had not intended to kill him, and he buried him in the sand. ﴿He said, "This﴾, his killing, ﴿is from the work of Satan﴾, the one who incites my anger. ﴿Indeed, he is an enemy﴾ to the children of Adam, ﴿misleading﴾ them, ﴿clearly misleading.﴾

﴿He said﴾ regretfully, ﴿"My Lord, I have wronged myself"﴾ by killing him, ﴿"so forgive me." So He forgave him﴾. ﴿Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾, i.e., the One characterized by both of them eternally, without beginning or end.

﴿He said, "My Lord, by what You have bestowed upon me"﴾ by the right of Your bestowal ﴿upon me﴾ by forgiveness, ﴿protect me, so I will never be a supporter﴾ (ظَهِيرًا), meaning an aid, ﴿to the criminals﴾, meaning the disbelievers, after this, if You protect me.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 18:

﴿So he woke in the city, fearful and watchful﴾, awaiting what might befall him because of the victim. ﴿Then behold, the man who had sought his help the day before called out to him for help﴾, crying out to him against another Egyptian. ﴿Moses said to him, "Indeed you are clearly misguided"﴾, evidently astray, because of what you did yesterday and today.

﴿Falamma an﴾, where *an* is *zā'idah* (an extra, non-essential particle), ﴿wanted to strike down the one who was an enemy to both of them﴾, that is, to Musa and the one who had sought his help. ﴿He said﴾, meaning the one who had sought help, thinking that Musa was going to strike him when he said to him, ﴿O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a person yesterday? You only want to be a tyrant in the land, and you do not want to be among the reformers﴾. The Coptic man heard this and knew that the killer was Musa. So he went to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and informed him of that, and Fir'awn ordered the slaughterers (*al-dhabbahīn*, the executioners) to kill Musa. They set out on the road toward him.

﴿And there came a man﴾, he being the believer from the family of Pharaoh, ﴿from the farthest part of the city﴾, its outskirts, ﴿running﴾, hastening in his walk by a route shorter than theirs. ﴿He said: "O Musa, the chiefs﴾ of Pharaoh's people ﴿are conspiring against you﴾, taking counsel about you ﴿to kill you, so leave﴾ the city. ﴿Indeed, I am to you one of the sincere advisers﴾ regarding the command to leave."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 21:

﴿So he left it, fearful, looking about in expectation.﴾ (He was awaiting) the pursuit of a pursuer, or God's aid to him. ﴿He said, "My Lord, deliver me from the wrongdoing people."﴾ That is, the people of Pharaoh.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 22:

﴿And when he turned toward﴾ he directed his face ﴿the way of Madyan﴾, toward its direction. It is the town of Shu'ayb, eight days' journey from Egypt. It was named after Madyan ibn Ibrahim. He did not know its route. ﴿He said, "It may be that my Lord will guide me to the right way."﴾ That is, the straight course of the road, the middle path leading to it. So God sent an angel to him holding a staff, and it set off with him toward it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 23:

﴿And when he arrived at the water of Madyan﴾, a well in which there were — i.e., he reached it — ﴿he found upon it a community﴾, a group ﴿of people watering﴾ their livestock; ﴿and he found apart from them﴾, besides them, ﴿two women holding back﴾, keeping back their sheep from the water. ﴿He said﴾, Musa said to them both, ﴿"What is your business?"﴾, what is your matter, that you do not water? ﴿They said, "We cannot water until the shepherds depart"﴾ — ri'a' (shepherds) is the plural of ra'in, i.e., they return from watering their flocks, out of fear of the crowding, ﴿so that we water﴾. And in another reading, yuṣdira is from the quadriliteral form, i.e., they turn their livestock away from the water. ﴿"And our father is an aged old man"﴾, who is unable to water.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 24:

﴿So he watered their flock for them﴾ from another well near them. He lifted a stone from it that no less than ten persons could lift. ﴿Then he withdrew﴾ he turned back ﴿to the shade﴾ of a samurah tree, because of the intense heat of the sun, and he was hungry. ﴿And said, "My Lord, indeed I am, for whatever good You send down to me, in need"﴾ of food, ﴿poor﴾ in need. So the two women returned to their father earlier than they usually did, and he asked them about that, and they informed him about the one who had watered their flock for them. So he said to one of them: "Call him to me."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 25:

﴿Then one of the two women came to him, walking bashfully.﴾ That is, holding the sleeve of her garment over her face out of modesty before him. ﴿She said: "Indeed my father invites you, so that he may reward you for your watering [the flocks] for us."﴾ He answered her, disapproving within himself of taking a wage, as though she had intended a recompense, if he was one who desired her. So she walked in front of him, and the wind kept blowing against her garment and uncovering her shins. He said to her: "Walk behind me and guide me to the way." She did so, until she came to her father, who was Shu'ayb (peace be upon him), and with him was supper. He said: "Sit down and eat supper." He said: "I fear that it may be a compensation for what you gave us to drink, and we are a household that does not ask for a return on a good deed." He said: "It is not my custom, nor the custom of my forefathers, to host a guest and not to feed the food." So he ate, and informed him of his situation.

﴿Then when he came to him and related to him the narrative,﴾ "al-qasas" is a verbal noun in the sense of the thing narrated: his killing of the Copt, their intention to kill him, and his fear of Pharaoh. ﴿He said: "Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people."﴾ For Pharaoh has no authority over the people of Madyan.

"One of the two women said: 'O father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one.'" (Here she is the one who was sent, the elder or the younger.) "O father, hire him" means: take him as a hired worker to tend our sheep in exchange for us. "Indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy one" means: hire him for his strength and his trustworthiness. So he (her father) asked her about him, and she informed him of what had preceded: his lifting the stone from the well, and his saying to her, "Walk behind me." Also, when she came to him and he knew of her, he lowered his head and did not raise it, so he became eager to marry him to her.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 27:

﴿He said: "I wish to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine"﴾, [namely] the elder or the younger, ﴿on condition that you hire yourself to me﴾, that you be a hired worker for me in pasturing my sheep, ﴿for eight years﴾, that is, years, ﴿and if you complete ten﴾, that is, pasture for ten years, ﴿then it is from you﴾, the completion, ﴿and I do not wish to burden you﴾ by stipulating the ten, ﴿you will find me, God willing﴾, for blessing, ﴿among the righteous﴾, those who fulfil the covenant.

Musa said: "That is between me and you. Whichever of the two terms I fulfill, let there be no injustice against me (in demanding more than it). And Allah is Witness over what we say," [Jalalayn's gloss: "Wakil" means Guardian or Witness.] So the contract was concluded on that basis. Shu'ayb instructed his daughter to give Musa a staff with which he could ward off predators from his sheep. The staffs of the prophets were with Shu'ayb, and there fell into her hand the staff of Adam, from the myrtle (aas) of Paradise, and Musa took it with Shu'ayb's knowledge.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 29:

﴿When Musa fulfilled the term﴾, i.e., his service, which was eight or ten years, and this is what is presumed; ﴿and set out with his family﴾, his wife, with the permission of her father, toward Egypt; ﴿he perceived﴾, i.e., he saw from a distance, ﴿from the side of the mount﴾, the name of a mountain, ﴿a fire. He said to his family: "Wait here,"﴾ [i.e., here]; ﴿"Indeed I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you news from it"﴾ about the way, for he had lost his way; ﴿"or a burning brand from the fire, that you may warm yourselves"﴾ — a piece and a flame; the jim may be vowelled with a fatha, a damma or a kasra (jadhwa, jadhwa, jidhwa); ﴿that you may warm yourselves﴾, i.e., that you may seek warmth; and the ta' is a substitute for the ta' of the iftiʿal form from ṣalā bil-nār (ṣalā, with the lam vowelled with a kasra or a fatha, meaning to be warmed by the fire).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 30:

﴿Then when he came to it, he was called from the right bank of the valley﴾ (shāti' — side, bank) ﴿in the blessed spot﴾ for Mūsā, because he heard the speech of Allah there ﴿from the tree﴾ — a substitute (badal) for "shāti'", with the preposition repeated because of the tree's growth in it; it was a tree of ʿunnāb (jujube), or ʿalīq, or ʿawsaj (hawthorn) ﴿that﴾ is explanatory (mufassira), not light (mukhaffafa).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 31:

﴿And throw down your staff.﴾ So he threw it down. ﴿Then when he saw it moving like it was a snake,﴾ writhing (tahtazz), ﴿as if it were a jann,﴾ and it was a small snake, because of the swiftness of its movement. ﴿He turned back, fleeing from it,﴾ running away from it, ﴿and did not return.﴾ That is, he did not come back. Then he was called out to.

﴿Insert﴾ (put in) ﴿your hand﴾ (al-yumna, the right) meaning the palm (al-kaff) ﴿into your bosom﴾ (jayb, the neck opening of the shirt), and draw it out; ﴿it will come out﴾ contrary to its former state of complexion (al-udmah), ﴿white, without any defect﴾, meaning leprosy (baras). So he inserted it and drew it out, and it shone like the rays of the sun that dazzle the sight. ﴿And draw your arm close to your side [wa-dmum ilayka janahaka] against fear﴾ (min al-rahab). The two letters of al-rahab may be read with a fatha on both, or with a fatha on the first and a sukun on the second, or with a damma on the first; the meaning is the fear that arises from the shining of the hand, by putting it into your bosom so that it returns to its original state. It was expressed by "wing" (janah) because for a person the arm is like the wing of a bird. ﴿Those two﴾ (fa-dhanika), with or without shadda, meaning the staff and the hand, both of which are feminine. The masculine demonstrative was used for them, and the subject, because its predicate is masculine (li-tadhkir khabarihi). ﴿Are two proofs﴾ (burhanan), sent (mursalan).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 33:

﴿He said: "My Lord, I have killed a soul among them, so I fear that they will kill me."﴾ He is the Copt mentioned earlier. ﴿so I fear that they will kill me﴾ for it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 34:

﴿And my brother Harun, he is more eloquent in tongue than me﴾, clearer (abyan), ﴿so send him with me as a supporter (ridan)﴾, helping (mu'inan). And in another recitation, with a fatha on the dal and without a hamza: ﴿he will confirm me (yusaddiqni)﴾, with a jazm (jussive), as a response to the supplication (jawab al-du'a'). And in another recitation, with a raf' (nominative), and its clause is a description (sifa) of ridan.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 35:

﴿He said, "We will strengthen your arm with your brother and give you both authority, so they will not reach you. Go, both of you, with Our signs; you and those who follow you will be the victors."﴾

[نُقَوِّيك] We will strengthen you
[بِأَخِيك] with your brother
[ونَجْعَل لَكُما سُلْطانًا] and We will give you both authority (sultan): dominance
[فَلا يَصِلُونَ إلَيْكُما] so they will not reach you both
[بِسُوءٍ] with harm
[اذْهَبا بِآياتِنا أنْتُما ومَن اتَّبَعَكُما الغالِبُونَ] Go with Our signs, you and those who follow you will be the victors
[لَهُمْ] over them

So when Moses came to them with Our signs, clear (wāḍiḥāt, a circumstantial qualifier of "bayyināt"), they said: "This is nothing but fabricated magic" (muftarā, i.e. invented, forged), "and we never heard of this" (kā'inan, i.e. occurring) "in" the days of our forefathers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 37:

﴿And Moses said⁠﴾ (with the waw and without it), ﴿"My Lord knows best⁠﴾ (ʿalīm, "knowing") ﴿who has come with guidance from Him⁠﴾ (the pronoun refers to the Lord), ﴿and whoever⁠﴾ (is a conjunction linking it to the preceding "man," i.e., "whoever") ﴿will have⁠﴾ (read with the taʾ (fawqāniyyah, "upper") and with the yāʾ (taḥtāniyyah, "lower")) ﴿the good outcome of the abode⁠﴾ (i.e., the praiseworthy outcome in the Hereafter), meaning: he (i.e., I) am in the right in both respects, so I am correct in what I have brought. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed⁠﴾ (the disbelievers).

﴿And Pharaoh said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than myself. So kindle for me, O Haman, [a fire] upon the clay, and make for me a tower﴾ — so bake for me the bricks (al-ājurr) — ﴿that I may look upon the God of Moses﴾, i.e., look at Him and ascertain Him, ﴿but indeed, I think he is among the liars﴾ in his claim of another god and that He sent him as a messenger.

And he and his soldiers were arrogant in the land, **the land of Egypt**, **without right**; and they thought that **they would not be returned to Us**. (*Al-bina' lil-fa'il wa lil-maf'ul*: the verb ﴿يُرْجَعُونَ﴾ may be read in the active voice, ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾, or the passive voice.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 28, verse 40:

﴿So We seized him and his soldiers, and cast them into the sea.﴾ "Cast them" means: We threw them. ﴿Into the sea﴾ meaning the salt sea, so they drowned. ﴿So look at how was the end of the wrongdoers.﴾ When they came to destruction.

﴿And We made them﴾ in this world ﴿leaders﴾ "أئمة" (a'immah), pronounced with the two hamzas both made clear, with the second changed to a yaa, chiefs in shirk (associating partners with God), ﴿calling to the Fire﴾ by their calling to shirk, ﴿and on the Day of Resurrection they will not be helped﴾ by having the punishment averted from them.

And We made them follow up (a curse) in this world (lanatan), (a) disgrace (khizyan), and on the Day of Resurrection they will be among the despised (al-maqbuhin), those removed far away (al-mub'adin).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 43:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾ the Torah ﴿after We had destroyed the former generations﴾ the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud and others ﴿as insights for mankind﴾ a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) from "the Book"; baṣāʾir is the plural of baṣīrah, which is the light of the heart, meaning lights for the hearts ﴿and a guidance﴾ from misguidance for whoever acts upon it ﴿and a mercy﴾ for whoever believes in it ﴿so that they may take heed﴾ admonish themselves by what it contains of admonitions.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 28, verse 44:

﴿And you were not﴾ O Muhammad ﴿on the western side﴾ of the mountain, or the valley, or the place ﴿of Musa, when﴾ he was called to converse ﴿We decreed﴾ i.e., We revealed ﴿to Musa the command﴾ of the mission to Pharaoh and his people ﴿and you were not among the witnesses.﴾ So that you would know it and report it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 45:

﴿But We produced generations﴾, nations, after Musa, ﴿and the life span grew long for them﴾; their lifetimes were prolonged, so they forgot the covenants, the sciences were effaced, and revelation ceased. ﴿So We sent you as a messenger﴾, and We revealed to you the story of Musa and others. ﴿And you were not a dweller﴾, residing ﴿among the people of Madyan, reciting to them Our verses﴾, a second report, ﴿so that you would know their history and then inform of it﴾. ﴿But We were sending messengers﴾ to you, and to you [came] reports of the earlier peoples.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 46:

﴿And you were not on the side of the Tur (the mountain)﴾ al-Jabal, ﴿when﴾ (idh) at the time when ﴿We called out﴾ to Musa, ﴿that take the Book with strength﴾; ﴿but﴾ (wa-lakin) ﴿We sent you as a mercy from your Lord, that you might warn a people to whom no warner had come before you﴾, and they are the people of Makkah, ﴿so that they may be mindful﴾ (la'allahum yatadhakkaruna), i.e., take admonition.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 47:

﴿And had it not been that a calamity should afflict them﴾ as a punishment ﴿for what their hands have sent forward﴾ of disbelief and other things ﴿they would say, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so that we might follow Your verses﴾ which he is sent with ﴿and be among the believers"﴾. The response to "lawla" (had it not been) is omitted, and what follows it is the subject (mubtada'). The meaning is: had it not been for the affliction and the statement that results from it, or had it not been for their statement that results from it, We would have hastened the punishment upon them; and [it is because] We have sent you to them as a messenger.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 48:

﴿When the Truth came to them from Us﴾, i.e. Muhammad, ﴿they said: "Why was he not given the like of what was given to Moses?"﴾ i.e. "Why has he not been given"? [They meant] of the signs, such as the white hand and the staff, and others, or of the Book all at once. ﴿Did they not disbelieve in what was given to Moses before?﴾ Where ﴿they said﴾ concerning it and concerning Muhammad: ﴿"Two sorcerers who back each other up"﴾, and in another reading "two magics" (siḥrān), i.e. the Qur'an and the Torah. ﴿They backed each other up﴾, i.e. they cooperated. ﴿And they said: "Surely we disbelieve in each﴾ of the two prophets and the two books."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 49:

﴿Say﴾ to them: ﴿Then bring a Book from Allah which is better guidance than these two﴾, than the two Books, ﴿that I may follow it, if you are truthful﴾ in what you claim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 50:

﴿Then if they do not respond to you﴾ to your call to bring a Book [like it], ﴿know that they only follow their own desires﴾ in their disbelief. ﴿And who is more astray than one who follows his own desire without guidance from Allah﴾ i.e., none is more astray than him. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 51:

﴿And We have certainly conveyed﴾ (i.e., We have explained) ﴿to them the word﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an) ﴿that they may be reminded﴾ (i.e., that they may take heed) ﴿and believe﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 52:

﴿Those to whom We gave the Book before it﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿they believe in it﴾ too. It was revealed concerning a group who embraced Islam from among the Jews, such as ʿAbdullah ibn Salam and others, and from among the Christians who came from Abyssinia (al-Habasha) and from al-Sham (Syria).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 28, verse 53:

﴿And when it is recited to them﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿they say, "We believe in it. Indeed, it is the truth from our Lord. Indeed, we were Muslims before it."﴾ monotheists (muwahhidin).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 54:

﴿Those are given their reward twice﴾ for their faith in both Books (al-Kitabayn, i.e., the Torah and the Gospel), ﴿because they were patient﴾ with their patience in acting upon both of them, ﴿and they repel﴾ they push back, ﴿evil with good﴾ i.e., they repel with good the evil done to them by others, ﴿and spend from what We have provided them﴾ they give in charity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 55:

﴿And when they hear vain talk﴾ — the abuse and harm from the disbelievers — ﴿they turn away from it and say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you."﴾ — a peace of disengagement; that is, "May you be safe from us, from abuse and otherwise." ﴿We do not seek the ignorant﴾ — we do not keep company with them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 56:

﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you love﴾ to his guidance. It was revealed concerning his (ﷺ) eagerness for the faith of his paternal uncle Abu Talib. ﴿But Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing﴾ of, knowing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 57:

﴿And they said﴾ — his people — ﴿"If we follow the guidance with you, we will be snatched away from our land."﴾ — we will be uprooted from it swiftly. ﴿"Have We not established for them a secure sanctuary"﴾ — in which they are safe from raids and killing, which occur between some Arabs and others — ﴿to which are brought﴾ — read with the feminine and the masculine ya' (taj-bi and yujba) — ﴿the fruits of all things,﴾ — i.e., from every direction — ﴿as provision﴾ — for them — ﴿from Us﴾ — from Our presence — ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ — that what We say is true.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 58:

﴿And how many a town We destroyed which exulted in its livelihood! So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little. And We were the inheritors.﴾ Its "livelihood" means its living (ʿaysh). By "town" is meant its people. ﴿So those are their dwellings, not inhabited after them except a little﴾ — except for passersby, for a day or part of a day. ﴿And We were the inheritors﴾ of them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 59:

﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns﴾ unjustly, while their people were righteous, ﴿until He had sent to their mother [town]﴾, i.e., the greatest of them, ﴿a messenger reciting to them Our verses. And We would never destroy the towns unless their people were wrongdoers﴾ through denying the messengers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 60:

﴿And whatever you have been given of things, it is the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment.﴾ You enjoy it and adorn yourselves with it during the days of your life, then it perishes. ﴿But what is with Allah﴾ i.e., His reward ﴿is better and more lasting. Do you not reason?﴾ With the ta' and the ya' (as two readings), that what remains is better than what perishes.

﴿Is one to whom We have made a good promise, and who will certainly meet it,﴾ meaning he will attain it, and it is Paradise, ﴿like one whom We have given the enjoyment of the life of this world,﴾ which will soon vanish, ﴿and then on the Day of Resurrection he will be among those brought forth?﴾ i.e., into the Fire. The first is the believer and the second is the disbeliever, i.e., they are not equal.
﴿And﴾ mention ﴿the Day when He calls to them﴾ [i.e., Allah] ﴿and says: "Where are My associates whom you used to claim?"﴾ [meaning] you used to claim them to be My associates.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 63:

﴿Those against whom the Word has been justified⦆ — by entry into the Fire — and they are the leaders of misguidance, ﴿said: "Our Lord, these are the ones whom we misguided; we misguided them just as we ourselves were misguided."⦆ — "These" is a subject (mubtada') and a qualifier (sifah), and ﴿we misguided them⦆ is its predicate (khabar), meaning: they went astray as we went astray. ﴿We did not compel them to error⦆ — ﴿we disavow before You⦆ — we disavow ourselves before You of them. ﴿They did not worship us⦆ — "ma" is a negation particle, and the object was placed first for the sake of the verse-ending (fasilah).

Note: the Qur'anic quotations are rendered in the translation above with the ﴿ ﴾ markers retained as requested; the bracketed symbols should be read as ﴿ ﴾ delimiters, and the translation here should be read as the rendering of the passage's Qur'anic words within those delimiters.

It is said: "Call upon your partners" — that is, the idols whom you claim to be God's partners. ﴿So they call upon them, but they do not respond to them﴾ — that is, to their calling. ﴿And they see the punishment﴾ — they witness it. ﴿If only they had been guided﴾ — in the world, so that they would not have seen what they see in the Hereafter.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti) on surah 28, verse 65:

﴿And﴾ [remember] ﴿the day He will call to them and say, "What was your response to the messengers?"﴾ [sent] to you.

﴿Then the news will be obscured from them﴾ the reports that would save them in reply, ﴿on that Day﴾, they will find no report in which there is salvation for them, ﴿and they will not question one another﴾ they will not question one another about it, so they will be silent.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 67:

﴿As for one who repents﴾ from polytheism, ﴿and believes﴾ affirms the Oneness of God, ﴿and does righteous deeds﴾ performs the obligatory duties, ﴿perhaps he will be among the successful﴾ the saved, by God's promise.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 68:

﴿And your Lord creates whatever He wills and chooses.﴾ Whatever He wills. ﴿They have no choice.﴾ For the polytheists, the choice (al-khiyara) in anything. ﴿Glorified is Allah and exalted above what they associate with Him.﴾ Above their associating (partners with Him).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 69:

﴿And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal﴾ (i.e., what their hearts keep hidden of disbelief and other than it) ﴿and what they disclose﴾ (i.e., with their tongues of that).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 70:

﴿And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs the praise in the first [life] ﴾ the worldly life ﴿and the Hereafter﴾ Paradise ﴿And to Him belongs the judgment﴾ the binding decree over everything ﴿And to Him you will be returned﴾ by resurrection.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 71:

﴿Say﴾ to the people of Makkah: ﴿Have you considered﴾, i.e., tell me, ﴿if Allah makes the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah﴾, i.e., according to your claim, ﴿who could bring you light﴾, i.e., daytime, in which you seek your livelihood? ﴿Will you not then listen﴾ with the listening of understanding, so that you would turn back from associating partners with Allah?

Say, [O Muhammad, to them]: "Have you considered: if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, who is a deity other than Allah [that could] bring you a night in which you rest?" That is, by your claim. "In it" [i.e., the night] you rest from fatigue. "Will you not then see" the error you are in, in associating partners [with Allah], so that you would turn back from it?

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 73:

﴿And of His mercy He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and that you may seek of His bounty﴾ — He, exalted is He, [made them] ﴿for you﴾ — i.e., in the night (﴿that you may rest therein﴾) — and ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾ — in the day, for earning — ﴿and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ for the blessing in both of them.
And mention ﴿the Day He will call to them, saying: "Where are My partners whom you used to claim?"﴾ He mentioned it a second time so that what follows may be built upon it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 75:

﴿And We shall draw out﴾ (wa-naza'na) we shall bring forth ﴿from every nation a witness﴾ and he is their prophet, who will testify against them concerning what they said. ﴿Then We shall say﴾ to them ﴿"Produce your proof"﴾ for what you claimed of association (ishrak). ﴿Then they will know that the truth﴾ concerning divinity ﴿belongs to Allah﴾ alone, ﴿none shares in it with Him﴾ anyone. ﴿And there will vanish from them﴾ (dalla), that is, be lost, ﴿what they used to invent﴾, and what they used to invent in the world, that He had a partner. Exalted is He above that.

Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa (﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Musa﴾), his paternal cousin (ibn ʿammihi) and his maternal cousin (ibn khālatihi), and he believed in him. ﴿So he transgressed against them﴾ with pride (al-kibr), haughtiness (al-ʿuluww) and abundance of wealth (wa-kathrat al-māl). ﴿And We gave him of the treasures such that its keys would indeed weigh down﴾ (tathqul, "would be heavy upon") ﴿a band of men﴾ (al-ʿuṣbah, "the group") ﴿of great strength﴾ (ūlī al-quwwah, "possessors of strength"). That is, the keys would weigh them down. The bāʾ in بِالعُصْبَةِ is the bāʾ of transitivity (al-bāʾ lil-taʿdiyah), which makes the verb transitive. Their number is said to be seventy, or forty, or ten, or other than that. ﴿Mention﴾ (udhkur) ﴿when his people said to him﴾ (al-muʾminūn min Banī Isrāʾīl, "the believers among the Children of Israel"): ﴿Do not exult﴾ (lā tafraḥ) ﴿in abundance of wealth﴾, for exultation here is farah baṭar (exultation with insolence). ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love those who exult﴾ (al-fariḥīn) ﴿in that﴾.

ﷻ﴿Wabtaghi﴾ (seek) ﴿fīmā ātāka Allāh﴾ — that is, of wealth — ﴿al-dār al-ākhirah﴾ (the Abode of the Hereafter), by spending it in obedience to God. ﴿Wa lā tansa﴾ (and do not forget), i.e., do not abandon, ﴿naṣībaka min al-dunyā﴾ (your share of the world), meaning that you should work in it for the Hereafter. ﴿Wa aḥsin﴾ (and be good) to people through charity, ﴿kamā aḥsana Allāh ilayka﴾ (as God has been good to you). ﴿Wa lā tabghi﴾ (and do not seek) ﴿al-fasād fī al-arḍ﴾ (corruption in the earth) by committing sins. ﴿Inna Allāh lā yuḥibbu al-mufsidīn﴾ (indeed God does not love the corrupters), meaning that He will punish them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 78:

﴿He said: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge I possess"﴾ i.e., the wealth, ﴿on account of knowledge I possess﴾ i.e., in return for it, and he was the most knowledgeable of the Children of Israel in the Torah after Musa and Harun. ﴿Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations﴾ nations ﴿that were greater than him in strength and greater in accumulation﴾ of wealth. i.e., he knows this, and Allah will destroy them. ﴿And the criminals will not be asked about their sins﴾ because of His exalted knowledge of them, so they will enter the Fire without reckoning.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 79:

﴿So he went out﴾ — Qarun — ﴿before his people in his adornment﴾, with his numerous followers, riding and adorned with garments of gold and silk, upon horses and mules that were decked out. ﴿Ya﴾ — this is for alerting — ﴿would that we had the like of what Qarun has been given﴾ in this world. ﴿Indeed, he is one of great fortune﴾ — a portion — ﴿great﴾ — abundant — in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 80:

﴿Those who had been given knowledge said﴾ to them, ﴿"Woe to you! The reward of Allah﴾ in the Hereafter, which is Paradise, ﴿is better for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ than what Qarun was given in the world. ﴿But none is granted it except the patient﴾ in obedience and in abstaining from disobedience. ﴿"

﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him﴾ [i.e., Qarun] ﴿and his dwelling﴾, ﴿and he had no company to help him against Allah﴾, i.e., other than Him, by preventing destruction from him. ﴿Nor was he among those who could defend themselves﴾ from Him.

And those who had wished to be in his place yesterday began to say (i.e., recently): ﴿Ah! It is as if Allah extends provision to whom He wills of His servants, and restricts it﴾ (yaqdir, i.e., straitens it) ﴿for whom He wills.﴾ The word ﴿وي﴾ (wai) is an ism fi'l (a verb-noun, an interjection-like verb) meaning "I am amazed" (a'jab), i.e., "I" (ana), and the kaf in ﴿ويْكَأَنَّ﴾ has the sense of the lam. ﴿Had Allah not been gracious to us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us up,﴾ read with the verb in the active (لَخَسَفَ) or the passive (لَخُسِفَ) form. ﴿Ah! It is as if the disbelievers do not prosper﴾ for the blessing of Allah, like Qarun.

That is the abode of the Hereafter: We shall assign it to those who do not desire haughtiness in the earth, by way of tyranny, nor corruption, by committing sins. And the praiseworthy end is for the God-fearing, those who guard against God's punishment by performing acts of obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 84:

﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, for him there is better than it﴾ — a reward on account of it, which is ten times its like. ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed, those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except﴾ a recompense ﴿for what they used to do﴾ — i.e., its equivalent.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 85:

﴿Indeed, He who has ordained the Qur'an upon you﴾ revealed it, ﴿will surely bring you back to a return﴾ to Makkah, and he (ﷺ) had longed for it. ﴿Say: My Lord knows best who has come with guidance and who is in manifest error﴾ It was revealed in reply to the statement of the disbelievers of Makkah to him: "Indeed you are in error." That is: he is the one who has come with guidance, and they are in error. And "a'lam" here means: "'alim" (knowing).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 28, verse 86:**

﴿You did not hope that the Book would be cast to you﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿except﴾ (but rather) it was cast to you ﴿as a mercy from your Lord. So do not be a supporter﴾ helper ﴿of the disbelievers﴾ in their religion, which they invited you to.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 28, verse 87:

﴿And let them not turn you away﴾ (wa-lā yaṣuddannaka). Its original form is yaṣuddūnanaka (yaṣuddūnanaka), the nūn of the raf' (indicative ending) was dropped because of the jāzim (apocopating particle, the negative prohibition lā), and the wāw (of the plural subject) was dropped because it met the sākin (unvocalized) nūn. ﴿from the signs of Allah after they have been sent down to you﴾, i.e., do not turn back to them in that matter. ﴿And call﴾ people ﴿to your Lord﴾ by affirming His oneness and worship of Him. ﴿And never be among the polytheists﴾ by assisting them. The jāzim did not affect the verb's ending because it is mabnī (built, i.e., having an invariable ending, as with the nūn of emphasis joined to it).

**Translation of Tafsir al-Jalalayn (Surah 28, verse 88):**

﴿And do not invoke﴾ worship ﴿with Allah another god. There is no god but Him. Everything is perishing except His Face﴾ except Him ﴿To Him belongs the judgment﴾ the executing decree ﴿and to Him you will be returned﴾ by resurrection from your graves.
